analysis.title: The US Fixed Income Weekly
key_insights: BofA frames recent market weakness as a risk repricing, not the start of a broader downturn. Higher rates, elevated volatility, geopolitical risk and heavy financing needs have widened credit spreads, but fundamentals remain resilient. US IG earnings are tracking +23.7% YoY, with core earnings ex Energy, Finance and Tech/AI up 7.0%.

The Oct FOMC press conference steepened the curve as markets questioned Warsh's resolve on inflation. 2-year yields fell 6bp and 30-year yields rose 4bp. BofA economists now expect 25bp hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027, with the terminal rate unchanged at 4.25-4.5%.

Rates team recommends staying paid 2y UST and in a 2s30s flattener ahead of midterms, labor data and refunding. Higher long-end yields raise the odds that Treasury cuts long-end auction sizes at next week's refunding, which would support 30-year swap spreads.

Technicals: the 10Y yield's decline from the 5.36% YTD high is viewed as a correction inside an uptrend. Support sits at 4.92-5.00%, with a possible extension to 4.83-4.81%. BofA favors fading lower yields and paying rates there. A sustained break below 4.74% would challenge the view.

US economics: the midterms are expected to have little effect on the outlook through 2028 because major legislation is unlikely. The baseline is a Democratic House and Republican Senate. A Republican sweep would add roughly 10-20bp to annual growth via defense spending. The main downside risk is state and local data center regulation.

BofA expects Oct NFP at +75k (private +70k) versus Bloomberg consensus of 65k, with the unemployment rate steady at 4.2%. 3Q GDP was 3.4% q/q saar, final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9%, and Sep core PCE was 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y.

Flow Show: higher bond yields are colliding with the AI capex boom. There have been 42 global central bank hikes in six months. Hyperscalers have issued $182bn of debt and $89bn of equity in 2026, and buybacks are running at $14bn YTD annualized versus $105bn in 2024. Hartnett recommends buying beaten-down tech bonds yielding 6-8%, with US tech bond relative returns versus IG at 30-year lows.

Hartnett sees risk-off until global hikes end and oil collapses in H1 2027. Key levels to hold before a year-end rally: MAGS $70 and SMH $520. YTD scores: oil 79.1%, US stocks 12.7%, bitcoin -8.4%, gold -7.1%.

IG credit: BofA expects spreads biased wider into year-end on supply overhang. November IG issuance is forecast at $175bn, and about $320bn of hyperscaler bond issuance is estimated through end-2027. Hyperscaler negative FCF should ease by 2028, so supply fears ease at some point in 2027. BBBs moved to neutral.
3Q earnings season: earnings +23.7% and revenue +9.1% YoY at the halfway point. Earnings beat by 2.9%, below 2Q's 8.2%. Weekly HG inflows were $4.35bn.

High yield and private credit: BofA expects a private credit recovery in 2027 driven by new vintages, while legacy stress drives a 7% default rate. New-issue spreads should widen about 20bp to 540bp. BofA favors private credit over private equity. AI-related credit issuance totals $572bn YTD. HY AI spreads tightened 69bp WTD to 376bp from a record 445bp.

Securitized products: overweight agency MBS. Non-QM AAA at about 155bp spread and 6.2% yield, and data center ABS/CMBS are preferred. Residual widening is possible over the next 1-3 weeks. 3Q nominal GDP growth slowed to 5.9% from 6.3%, which supports a near-term 10y rally toward 4.75%. Non-agency RMBS issuance is a post-GFC record $232bn YTD.
CMBS: neutral, but BofA would use widening to add high-quality floating-rate SASB and CRE CLOs. Data center CMBS widened 5-40bp this week.

ABS: spreads are rangebound with a wider bias. Preferred sectors are solar, data center, aircraft, fiber, railcar and franchise/whole-business. YTD issuance is $336.2bn, with a $407bn full-year forecast.

CLOs: AAAs are attractive as floaters in a volatile rate environment. Headwinds are heavy competing issuance and softer loans, with 13.1% of the US loan market trading below 80. CLO equity distributions are weak.

Municipals: the best value has shifted to the long end. The 10s30s curve is 139bp, and 2027 principal plus coupons of $692bn exceed the $650bn issuance forecast by $42bn. October IG muni returns are 3.22% MTD, potentially the best October on record. Voters will consider $168bn+ of bond authorizations on Election Day.

Europe and EM: European credit has repriced about four standard deviations. BofA is cautious on France fiscal stress, and downgrades Brazil external debt to Marketweight after Lula's reelection. Asian currencies are tied to AI risk appetite, with TWD at 53% correlation to AI equities. USD/KRW is forecast at 1330 at year-end.

Funding: repo rose into October month-end on a higher TGA, bill issuance and Canadian year-end. BofA expects the Fed to restart reserve management purchases at about $10bn a month in mid-November, and supports long Dec 2026 SOFR/FF.

Metals: copper is tight, with record Shanghai premiums and LME backwardation, despite China consumption down 8% YoY in September. Data center electricity demand is projected to rise from 548 TWh in 2026 to 1,025 TWh by 2030.

sector_views.rationale: Spreads are biased wider into year-end on heavy November supply of about $175bn and hyperscaler issuance. BBBs moved to neutral. Pipelines, insurance, utilities and energy are preferred, and consumer products and healthcare are underweight.
Technicals are improving with lower near-term production and slower premium prepayments.
Non-QM AAA at about 155bp spread and 6.2% yield offers value after widening.
Use weakness to add high-quality floating-rate SASB and CRE CLOs.
The long end offers value after a steep 10s30s curve, and 2027 redemptions exceed issuance.
Relative return versus IG is near 30-year lows with yields of 6-8% as hyperscalers shift funding toward equity and debt issuance.
Higher debt-service costs and AI disruption of software portfolios weigh on private equity.

earnings_insights: BofA tracks 3Q US IG issuer earnings at +23.7% YoY and revenue at +9.1% YoY at the halfway point, reported basis. Earnings beat expectations by 2.9% versus 8.2% in 2Q.
Alphabet (GOOGL) 3Q26 revenue rose 25% YoY to $128bn, reported. 2026 capex guidance is unchanged at $195-205bn, with a significant increase expected in 2027. Free cash flow was negative.
Amazon (AMZN) quarterly capex was $76bn, with FY capex guidance unchanged at $220bn. AWS backlog is a record $578bn. Free cash flow was negative.
Microsoft (MSFT) cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9bn. Quarterly capex was $45bn, lower than expected, with $50bn guided for fiscal Q2 2027.
AerCap (AER) raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to about $20.70.
OneMain (OMF) now expects managed receivables growth of 9% versus the prior 6-9%, and net charge-offs at the high end of the 7.4-7.9% range.
SoFi (SOFI) reported record originations of $16.9bn. Pagaya (PGY) guided 4Q26 network volume of $2.961-3.261bn versus $3.6bn in 3Q26.
Hilton Grand Vacations (HGV) said sales fell short of expectations and lowered contract sales and VPG forecasts. Travel + Leisure (TNL) raised full-year gross VOI sales guidance to $2.625-2.675bn.

Chart 2 shows US IG tech bond relative returns versus US IG bonds at 30-year lows.
vol_and_positioning: Rates team keeps a long forward-vol bias, favoring longer-tenor over front-end volatility alongside curve-flattening option structures.
The 2Y and 5Y are near CTA short-cover levels. CTA short covering could temporarily extend the rally.
VIX at 17, down from 19.03 a week earlier.
Hartnett's Bull & Bear Indicator slipped to 7.1.
HG inflows were $4.35bn and HY returned to inflows, while loans posted their largest outflow since March.
CDX IG at 61bp and CDX HY at 106.
geopolitical: US midterm elections next week, with a Democratic House and Republican Senate as the baseline.
Iran tensions are a continuing upside risk to energy prices and inflation, and hedging Iran risk is getting expensive.
A re-escalation of hostilities in the Middle East could delay a CMBS recovery.
France fiscal stress and yield deterioration raise contagion and ECB intervention risk.
Lula's reelection in Brazil raises fiscal risk and weakens BRL.
Governments increasingly pay a mineral-security premium via stockpiles, subsidies and trade measures.

tension_points.bull_case: A dovish hold keeps rates orderly and supports muni and securitized performance. Spreads should tighten once volatility falls.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed is reactive on inflation. The press conference drove a twist-steepening with wider long-end breakevens, and the Fed could fall behind the curve with 25-50bp more hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained 10Y break below 4.74% would challenge the bearish-yield thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: AI earnings are strong, hyperscaler FCF should improve by 2028, and beaten-down tech bonds offer 6-8% yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex surging to $1.2tn in 2027 drives heavy issuance and weak FCF, and any profitability shortfall could trigger a correction hitting investment, Asian exports and consumption.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Large hyperscaler new-issue deals in November would keep the supply overhang in place.

tension_points.bull_case: Widening and higher risk-free yields improve long-term value, and election clarity could be an earlier catalyst for tightening.
tension_points.bear_case: Residual widening is possible over the next 1-3 weeks, and a Middle East escalation would delay recovery.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Re-escalation of hostilities in the Middle East.
